questions.q: What does the acronym SOAR stand for?
options: Systematic Observation and Response
Security Operations and Alert Reporting
Security Orchestration and Review
Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response
questions.explain: SOAR breaks into three distinct capabilities: orchestration, automation, and response.

questions.q: What does orchestration specifically mean in a SOAR platform?
options: Replacing the SIEM entirely
Writing the actual detection rules a SIEM uses
Manually copying data between tools by hand
Connecting a SOC's separate tools, like the SIEM, EDR, and threat intel feed, through their APIs so data and actions flow between them
questions.explain: Orchestration is the connective layer that lets a SOAR platform talk to multiple existing security tools automatically.

questions.q: How does automation differ from orchestration in SOAR?
options: Automation replaces the need for any tool integration
Automation only applies to writing SIEM correlation rules
Automation runs a defined sequence of steps without a human doing each one every time, using the connections orchestration provides
Automation and orchestration mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: Orchestration makes the connection between tools possible; automation is what actually uses that connection to run steps without a human.

questions.q: What makes the 'Response' part of SOAR different from what a SIEM alone does?
options: A SIEM already takes automated response actions, so SOAR adds nothing new
Response only applies to email security tools
The platform can carry out a real action itself, like isolating a host, instead of only raising an alert and waiting for a human
Response just means sending a louder alert notification
questions.explain: A SIEM detects and alerts; SOAR's response capability lets the platform actually act -- block, quarantine, or isolate.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say SOAR is becoming increasingly necessary for SOCs?
options: SOAR is required by a specific compliance regulation covered elsewhere in this course
Alert volume keeps climbing while analyst headcount grows far more slowly, creating alert fatigue that automation helps offset
SOCs no longer need any human analysts once SOAR is in place
Alert volume has been declining, making manual triage easier each year
questions.explain: The growing gap between alert volume and analyst headcount produces alert fatigue, which SOAR addresses by automating the repeatable portion of the workload.
